questions.stem: A QServer has maxSessions 200, and its channel's timeout property is set to 0. A firewall in front of it drops idle flows after 20 minutes without telling either end. Every night about 30 terminals lose their flow this way and reconnect in the morning. What do terminals see after about a week?

options.text: New connections are refused while connected terminals keep working, since each lost session still holds a thread from the pool
options.says: with the read timeout disabled a silently dropped session never ends; once 200 are held, ISOServer closes its listening socket and refuses new connections, while existing sessions go on

options.text: New connections are refused and connected terminals stop too, since the server stops serving once its pool runs out
options.says: only the listening socket is closed; the sessions that hold the threads keep working

options.text: Every terminal keeps working, since the server closes the old session when the same terminal connects again
options.says: QServer knows connections, not terminals; a reconnect opens a new session and leaves the old one

options.text: Every terminal keeps working, since the server ends each dead session after its five-minute default
options.says: 300000 ms is the default only when the property is absent; 0 disables the read timeout

origin.section: 3.1 Every Connection Holds a Thread Until It Closes

questions.stem: A listener placed before IncomingListener calls a fraud service and answers each purchase itself; the call takes 3 seconds. Terminal 29110055 sends three purchases back to back on its connection, and at the same moment terminal 29110056 sends one on another connection. When does the last answer reach each terminal?

options.text: 29110055 after about 9 s and 29110056 after about 3 s, since a session reads its next message only after the listener returns
options.says: the session thread is the connection's only reader, so 29110055's purchases are handled one after another; the other connection has its own session

options.text: 29110055 after about 9 s and 29110056 after about 9 s, since one listener object handles the calls of every connection one at a time
options.says: the one listener instance is called by every session concurrently; it does not serialise connections

options.text: 29110055 after about 3 s and 29110056 after about 3 s, since QServer starts a new thread for each message it reads
options.says: QServer has one thread per connection, not per message

options.text: 29110055 after about 3 s and 29110056 after about 3 s, since each purchase waits only for its own call to the fraud service
options.says: a purchase also waits for every purchase before it on the same connection

origin.section: 3.3 A Listener Holds Up Its Own Connection

questions.stem: After a firmware update, the purchases a terminal sends can no longer be unpacked by the server's packager. The QServer uses ASCIIChannel and the default server properties. The terminal sends such a purchase and, right behind it on the same connection, an 0420 for an earlier purchase. What becomes of the two messages?

options.text: Neither is answered, since the session ends at the bad frame and never reads the 0420
options.says: without ignore-iso-exceptions an unpack error ends the session and closes the connection, losing what follows

options.text: Neither is answered, since the server holds the 0420 until the purchase is sent again in a valid form
options.says: the server holds nothing back; the connection is closed

options.text: The 0420 is answered, since the session drops only the bad frame and goes on reading
options.says: that is what ignore-iso-exceptions does; by default the session ends

options.text: The 0420 is answered, since the server first returns an error response for the purchase
options.says: a frame that can't be unpacked gets no answer at all

origin.section: 3.4 A Frame the Server Can't Unpack Ends the Connection

questions.stem: A TLS QServer's server-socket-factory sets clientauth to true and leaves every other trust setting at its default. Its keystore holds the server's key and the certificate of the acquirer's terminal CA. A laptop on the store network connects with a self-signed certificate it made itself. What happens?

options.text: The laptop gets in and can send requests, since nothing on the server compares the certificate with a trusted CA
options.says: the 2.1.7 factory checks certificates against the keystore only with serverauth=true; otherwise it trusts any certificate

options.text: The laptop gets in and can send requests, since a self-signed certificate vouches for itself and so counts as trusted
options.says: self-signing does not make a certificate trusted; it got in only because nothing checked it

options.text: The laptop is refused during the handshake, since the server compares the certificate with the CA it trusts
options.says: clientauth only asks for a certificate; checking it needs serverauth

options.text: The laptop is refused during the handshake, since a certificate that no CA signed fails the TLS handshake
options.says: whether a certificate is accepted is up to the trust manager, and the default one here accepts any

origin.section: 3.6 A TLS Server Checks Client Certificates Only With `serverauth`
